Nonconventional cash flows can have multiple IRRs.

deferred.title: Uneven raw-cash-flow net present value in a single expression
deferred.reason: Corporate Issuers LM4 printed pp737–739/PDF pp751–753, equations 1–2: the full arbitrary-time raw-cash-flow formula requires elementwise discounting of indexed cash flows before summation, which the present family grammar cannot express directly. Existing Volume 1 cash-flow additivity supports a precomputed same-date value family and the supplied lump-sum model discounts each element externally.

models.title: Fixed coupon bond price at a flat periodic yield
models.summary: Bond proceeds are the present value of the coupon annuity plus the present value of principal.

relationship.expression: coupon * (1 - (1 + rate) ** (-periods)) / rate + face / (1 + rate) ** periods
relationship.original_equation: Bond price = present value of level coupons + present value of face value
relationship.translation_notes: The rate is per coupon period and base one; the number of periods is a dimensionless count. Coupon and principal are in one currency. This combines two supplied time-value primitives into a distinct bond-price quantity.

assumptions: Coupons are equal and paid at the end of each of the stated positive integer number of periods; face is paid at the final coupon date.
One flat effective discount rate applies to all periods and there are no transaction costs.
limitations: The closed form excludes a zero periodic rate; its separate continuous limit is coupon times periods plus face.
Fractional-period pricing, default, embedded options, taxes and term-structure variation require other models.
Integer period count is a documented domain requirement; the scalar grammar cannot enforce integrality.
